'''Daniela De Angelis MBE''' is an Italian biostatistician specializing in infectious disease modelling. Her current roles are Professor of Statistical Science for Health at the [[University of Cambridge]] in the Department of Primary Care and Public Health and Deputy Director and Programme Leader at the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom) | Medical Research Council]] [[Biostatistics]] Unit.<ref name="mrcbsu">{{Cite web|url=https://www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk/people/in-alphabetical-order/a-to-g/daniela-de-angelis/|title=Daniela De Angelis|website=www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk|access-date=2022-11-04|archive-date=2022-11-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221104145144/https://www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk/people/in-alphabetical-order/a-to-g/daniela-de-angelis/|url-status=live}}</ref> She has published research on the development and application of statistical methods to monitor infectious diseases such as SARS COVID-19, influenza, HIV and hepatitis C. De Angelis is a member of scientific advisory groups such as [[NICE]], [[WHO]], and [[UNAIDS]]. She is a member of SPI-M (Scientific Pandemic Influenza Advisory Committee, subgroup on Modelling) and the [[Royal Statistical Society]] Task Force for COVID-19.<ref name="mrcbsu" /> In 2022, she was awarded an Honorary MBE for her services to Medical Research and Public Health.<ref>https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/honorary-british-awards-to-foreign-nationals-2022/honorary-awards-to-foreign-nationals-in-2022</ref>

== Career history ==

In 2017, the [[Contaminated blood scandal in the United Kingdom#2017_–_Legal_action_and_UK_public_inquiry|Infected Blood Inquiry]] was launched.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-07-11 |title=Theresa May orders contaminated blood scandal inquiry |url=http://www.theguardian.com/society/2017/jul/11/contaminated-blood-scandal-theresa-may-orders-inquiry |access-date=2023-01-20 |website=the Guardian |language=en |archive-date=2023-01-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230117102525/https://www.theguardian.com/society/2017/jul/11/contaminated-blood-scandal-theresa-may-orders-inquiry |url-status=live }}</ref> De Angelis is a member of the Statistics Expert Group as part of this inquiry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Expert Groups {{!}} Infected Blood Inquiry |url=https://www.infectedbloodinquiry.org.uk/about/inquiry-experts |access-date=2023-01-20 |website=www.infectedbloodinquiry.org.uk |archive-date=2022-10-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007130221/https://www.infectedbloodinquiry.org.uk/about/inquiry-experts |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2019, De Angelis was appointed Professor of Statistical Science for Health at the University of Cambridge.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2018-19/weekly/6557/section3.shtml|title=Notices by the General Board - Cambridge University Reporter 6557|website=www.admin.cam.ac.uk|access-date=2022-11-04|archive-date=2023-01-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230120103549/https://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2018-19/weekly/6557/section3.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Research ==
=== HIV ===
In HIV modelling, De Angelis was the senior author of a study that projected that England would diagnose 95% of people living with HIV by 2025.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/hiv-england-cases-treatment-latest-b1925773.html | title=England set to eradicate HIV by 2030, research suggests | website=[[Independent.co.uk]] | date=24 September 2021 | access-date=14 November 2022 | archive-date=14 November 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114123704/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/hiv-england-cases-treatment-latest-b1925773.html | url-status=live }}</ref> This is one of three aspects of UNAIDS' 90-90-90 goal: to have 90% of people with HIV diagnosed, 90% of people diagnosed with HIV receiving antiretroviral therapy and 90% of people receiving this therapy having viral suppression.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unaids.org/en/resources/909090|title=90-90-90: treatment for all|website=www.unaids.org|access-date=2022-11-14|archive-date=2020-05-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200514013609/https://www.unaids.org/en/resources/909090|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== COVID-19 ===
De Angelis was the senior statistician for the MRC Biostatistics Unit's "nowcasting" and forecasting of COVID-19 data: using statistical modelling to estimate current (and predict future) numbers of infections, [[Basic_reproduction_number#Effective_reproduction_number|''R''<sub>t</sub>]], numbers of hospital admissions and more, by age and region in England.<ref name="nowcasting">{{cite web | url=https://www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk/tackling-covid-19/nowcasting-and-forecasting-of-covid-19/ | title=Nowcasting and Forecasting of the COVID-19 Pandemic | access-date=2022-11-14 | archive-date=2022-11-14 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114125308/https://www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk/tackling-covid-19/nowcasting-and-forecasting-of-covid-19/ | url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Real-time nowcasting and forecasting of COVID-19 dynamics in England: the first wave|first1=Paul|last1=Birrell|first2=Joshua|last2=Blake|first3=Edwin|last3=van Leeuwen|first4=Nick|last4=Gent|first5=Daniela|last5=De Angelis|date=July 19, 2021|journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences|volume=376|issue=1829|article-number=20200279|doi=10.1098/rstb.2020.0279|pmid=34053254|pmc=8165585}}</ref> This information was provided directly to the SAGE sub-group, SPI-M and to regional teams at the [[UK Health Security Agency]] (UKHSA).<ref name="nowcasting" />

== Recognition ==

In 2018, De Angelis received the [[Suffrage Science award|Suffrage Science Award]] in Maths & Computing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.suffragescience.org/m-c-2018-award-handover|title=M&C 2018 AWARD HANDOVER|website=suffragescience|access-date=2022-11-04|archive-date=2022-11-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221104145143/https://www.suffragescience.org/m-c-2018-award-handover|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

In 2021, she received the University of Cambridge Vice-Chancellor's Established Academic Award for her work on real-time monitoring of the SARS-COV2 pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.research-strategy.admin.cam.ac.uk/impact/vice-chancellors-awards/vice-chancellors-awards-2021|title=Vice Chancellor's Awards 2021|first=Helen|last=Gaughan|date=March 3, 2022|website=www.research-strategy.admin.cam.ac.uk|access-date=November 4, 2022|archive-date=November 4, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221104145149/https://www.research-strategy.admin.cam.ac.uk/impact/vice-chancellors-awards/vice-chancellors-awards-2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2022, De Angelis was awarded an honorary MBE for services to medical research and public health.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/honorary-british-awards-to-foreign-nationals-2022/honorary-awards-to-foreign-nationals-in-2022|title=Honorary awards to foreign nationals in 2022|website=GOV.UK|access-date=2022-11-04|archive-date=2022-10-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221012155316/https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/honorary-british-awards-to-foreign-nationals-2022/honorary-awards-to-foreign-nationals-in-2022|url-status=live}}</ref> That same year, she also received the [[Weldon Memorial Prize]] as a member of the Scientific Pandemic Influenza Group on Modelling, Operational sub-group (SPI-M-O).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/event/modelling-covid-19-pandemic-uk-weldon-memorial-prize-lecture-2022|title=Modelling the Covid-19 Pandemic in the UK: The Weldon Memorial Prize Lecture 2022 &#124; University of Oxford|website=www.ox.ac.uk|access-date=2022-11-04|archive-date=2023-01-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230120103552/https://www.ox.ac.uk/event/modelling-covid-19-pandemic-uk-weldon-memorial-prize-lecture-2022|url-status=live}}</ref>
